sentences.text: 2. Heard Shri Manvendra Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri S.B. Maurya, learned counsel for the State and perused the material brought on record 3.

The present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant-Jitendra Pratap Singh with the prayer to allow this application and quash the entire criminal proceeding of Case No.
744 of 2019 (State Vs. Jitendra Pratap Singh) arising out of case crime no.832 of 2017, u/s 419, 420,
467, 468, 471, 352, 504, 506 IPC, P.S. Meerganj, Jaunpur pending before Civil Judge (J.D.)/F.T.C.
Jaunpur and charge sheet dated 27.8.2018 and cognizance order and summoning order dated 28.5.2019 passed by J.M.-II, Jaunpur and further to stay the further proceeding, charge sheet along with cognizance order as aforesaid during the pendency of present application before this Hon'ble Jitendra Pratap Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191517062/
1 Court.

entities.text: Jitendra Pratap Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is argued that the present criminal prosecution is nothing but an exercise in futility.

5. After having heard learned counsel for the parties and perusing the records, it is apparent that there are number of factual controversies involved in the matter, which could be well appreciated only by the trial court.
Since the applicant is not bailed out as yet, he shall appear before the trial court within 15 days from today and move an application u/s 88 Cr.P.C.
The trial court, after ensuring the presence of the applicant, shall release him with or without sureties.
Said application shall be decided within 15 days thereafter.

Thereafter, the applicant shall move an application seeking discharge u/s 227/239 Cr.P.C., which would be heard and decided by the trial court within six weeks from its filing by a well reasoned order after hearing learned counsel for the State.
6. Till the disposal of said discharge application moved on behalf of applicant, he shall not be arrested in aforesaid case crime.

7. It is made clear that in the event the 'Discharge Application' is decided against the applicant, then it would be incumbent upon the applicant that he would surrender before the trial court concerned and file a bail application.
8. This application stands disposed off with above observations.

(Samit Gopal, J.) Order Date :- 21.4.2023 Gaurav  Jitendra Pratap Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191517062/
